claims.text: Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is a disordered single-phase BCC alloy.
Equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo has a room-temperature compressive yield strength of approximately 1719 MPa.
The limited plasticity of equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo is primarily caused by the electronegativity disparity introduced by its high Mo content.
V has lower electronegativity than Mo.
Replacing 5–7 at.% of Mo with V will reduce the alloy's overall electronegativity disparity.
Partial replacement of Mo by V will preserve refractory-element solid-solution strengthening.
Vacuum arc melting followed by homogenization near 1200 °C for several hours will produce a uniform disordered BCC NbZrTiHfMo-V alloy.
At an optimized V level, the modified alloy will retain a single-phase disordered BCC structure.
V substitution will subtly modify the BCC lattice parameter.
Reducing electronegativity disparity by replacing Mo with V will alleviate local bonding inhomogeneity and strong local bonding contrast.
Reduced local bonding contrast will promote more uniform dislocation motion.
More uniform dislocation motion will enhance room-temperature compressive plasticity while refractory solid-solution strengthening maintains high strength.
The optimized V-substituted alloy will have a room-temperature compressive yield strength near or slightly above 1700 MPa.
The optimized V-substituted alloy will show a 20–30% increase in compressive plastic strain relative to equiatomic NbZrTiHfMo.
The beneficial effect is limited to V substitution levels that preserve a single-phase disordered BCC structure, likely below approximately 10 at.% V.
Exceeding approximately 10 at.% V may cause phase instability or second-phase formation that degrades mechanical performance.

contradictions.description: The formula NbZrTiHfMo_(1-x)V_x with x = 0.05–0.07 does not correspond to 5–7 at.% V in the full alloy after normalization; it gives roughly 1–1.4 at.% V. Elsewhere, 5, 7, and 10 are explicitly described as total atomic-percent replacement levels.
The hypothesis says strength will not be compromised relative to a 1719 MPa baseline, whereas a prediction merely near 1700 MPa permits a reduction below that baseline.
